answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: before an agent can transact, it locks a deposit in a common vault. Honest service earns the deposit back, but proven fraud forfeits it, so spawning ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand deposits rather than ten thousand votes. A public mirror of deposits and past conduct lets any peer verify an account's standing, and a sable seal on the record marks stake that has survived a full audit period without cheating.
